_about: Rules for the Flow, cover and Cleanup audits, which run on backward chains (steam_layout/chains.py, covers.py, cleanups.py). The stacks are derived from the layout; this file only declares what bindings can't say: the starting contexts the chains may begin from (Base alone, and Base with the stateful Gyro layer on it), which layers are covers, and the exceptions register. Titles use default-layout names; 'variants' maps them for the alternative layout. Until 2026-10-01 this file also declared a 'families' section for the family walk (deprecated); that version is kept as archived/depth-search-and-family-walk/tests/data/flow_families_90.9.json.

covers._about: Cover-type layers (Layer Definition of Done section 5). They inherit their owner, so differing lower bindings are expected; the cover check (covers.py) judges them instead.

exceptions_about: The exceptions register (steam_layout/exceptions.py): every place where the layout breaks a rule and that is accepted (status allow) or is a known gap a to-do will close (status todo). Each entry names its rule (resources/Layer Definition of Done.md), what it covers, why, who decided it and when, and the to-do that ends it. Until 2026-10-02 these lived in four shapes: 'decisions', 'covers.allow' and 'cleanups.keep' here, and per-target decisions in traced_stacks.json. An entry that matches nothing is reported as stale by the audit that reads it.

exceptions.why: Documented steering design: helpers inherit the active W/S owner's driver bindings so the dominant press, owner release and takeover work in every phase (findings/2026-09-30-steering-lean/README.md, reused single-side covers; pinned by test_dominant_two_entries_inherit_through_every_helper).

exceptions.why: A cover inherits its owner, so different bindings below it are expected, and the cover check (R144) judges it. Its inherited inputs are not reviewed one by one; without this, changing one Tap Cover brings 15 to 18 entries.

scope.note: Four hold_layer commands in each layout: LTP: Arrow Keys, RTP: Mouse Buttons, LTP: Middle Click and RTP: Middle Click each hold themselves on a Soft Press of the pad click. add_layer puts them on; the hold is there to take them off.

exceptions.why: The author's exception for the trackpad click layers: the hold tracks the removal at the Soft Press threshold, and the inverted repeating Soft Press removal stays behind it as the backup, because holds are unreliable.

scope.note: A pair is set aside when either layer is a touchpad layer (every binding that adds it is on a trackpad) or the covered exit is a trackpad input. 68 pairs on 90.13, 71 on 90.14 and 90.15, 99 on 90.16: the pad click layers gained a touch Release, which the Double Tap windows cover as they cover the other pad layers' (31 pairs), and they now carry the touch Release of the three right-pad layers under them (3 fewer).

exceptions.why: The windows clear both pads' touch, so a thumb leaving a pad inside a window misses a pad layer's Release; RTP: Double Tap binds the buttons whose Releases other layers need. The fixes are proposed, not decided.

scope.note: Steering's 1.5 s hold exit, Cursor Gyro's both-sticks exit and the Modifier 2 clear leave a stateful layer without a transition. Cursor Gyro's entry also adds Gyro underneath.

exceptions.why: Extra exits are allowed; the menu-plus-click clear and the Modifier 2 clear are never dropped.

scope.note: Gamepad isn't left by the Modifier 2 quick tap. Its bumpers and triggers are gamepad buttons, so no modifier layer exists there; it is left only by a menu button held plus a stick click.

exceptions.why: The author, asking for the layer: the bumpers can't be the way out of Gamepad, 'it just doesn't make any sense'. This settles the older to-do that kept Gamepad through the clear.

Since 90.21 Steering's two Entry Points serve every stateful layer and are named Stateful. They follow the layer they are on: over Cursor Gyro a right-pad touch adds RTP: Entry Point from Base, as it does under Base's own Entry Points; over Steering it does nothing, because Steering clears that touch on purpose.

exceptions.why: Gamepad binds every input, so no layer can be added over it (R168), and Long Press and Double Press only misbehave with layers (A20). Start and Select there use Steam's own activators instead of window and cover layers: an interruptible Regular Press sends the button, a Double Press holds it, a Long Press is empty and swallows the tap. Rests on A43 and A44.

scope.note: Gamepad has no Entry Points. A chord on each stick click, on Start or Select being held, runs the Entry Points' clear list and adds the clear transition. It fires at the click's press, not its Release.

exceptions.why: The author asked for no helper layers in Gamepad. An Entry Point would be a layer over Gamepad, which the Long Press and Double Press on its menu buttons rule out (R168). If the menu button is let go before the stick click, Base is live under a held click and may type one Q or E (A11).
exceptions.decided: Proposed in plans/2026-10-03-cursor-gyro-and-gamepad.md; the author told me to build it, 2026-10-03

scope.note: Gamepad's Start and Select each have a Long Press, which is a delayed binding on a menu button at entry.

exceptions.why: The commit is the menu button's own Release, so that button is up when Gamepad lands and its Long Press can't be running. Only a second menu button still held at the commit lands in Gamepad held, and may send its button once (A10).
exceptions.decided: Proposed in plans/2026-10-03-cursor-gyro-and-gamepad.md; the author told me to build it, 2026-10-03

exceptions.why: Each menu stick guard handles only its own stick. It leaves the other stick's edge open, so the Entry Point's add of the other guard still comes through.
Each menu stick guard handles only its own stick. It leaves the other stick's edge open, so the Entry Point's add of the other guard still comes through.

The left stick being out is what keeps these two layers on, and its edge Release is their exit, so nothing can guard a cleanup function there. Their cleanup function goes on the right-stick edge, guarded by the left stick being out.

Since 90.24 the cover has a right-stick group in mouse mode, for its stick-touch cleanup (R169). Over a layer whose right stick is in D-pad mode nothing on that stick is inherited (A2), so the cover hides this exit. The cover is only on while the right thumb rests on the right pad, and the hidden inputs need that thumb on the right stick. A stale cover removes itself on the right-stick touch. Called out by the author: while the thumb is on the pad, a menu button plus the right-stick click does not start a transition, in the Entry Points and in the Fn layers that inherit that click.

The guards bind only the menu buttons and the sticks, so the bumpers and triggers come from the Entry Point underneath. Since 90.24 each of those carries the Entry Point's cleanup function (R171), whose chord and list name that Entry Point, so the input differs between the four. The player sees the same thing in every stack: with the menu button held the input does what it did, and with it not held the stale menu layers are removed.
